title: THESES 6 AND 7
rule: Every implication requires a separately named input, judgment, and authority.
needs: a check of fidelity to the intended statement
fails: a distributed computation can finish without error while producing no mathematical object
a kernel can accept a proof of a statement that is not the statement intended
a valid result can rest on a premise whose status does not permit promotion
a promoted result can still lack the authority to be published
who: Retrieval may supply candidate evidence but cannot change truth status.
broken: a worker can write directly to the status store
an evaluator shares mutable code or keys with the candidate
a signature is detached from the artifact hash
a promotion service accepts a producer's boolean assertion instead of replayable receipts
verdict: the proposition does not apply and the system has failed its constitution
